payload.task_text:
The product team wants to analyze customer review quality across product categories to prioritize product improvement efforts. Query WooCommerce product review data and link it to product categories to understand how different categories perform with customers.

Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Category Analysis" with columns: Category, Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating (rounded to 2 decimal places), Five_Star_Count, and Five_Star_Rate (the percentage of reviews that are 5 stars, rounded to 1 decimal). Sort by Category alphabetically. The second sheet should be called "Top Products" and list the top 10 highest-rated products that have at least 3 reviews, with columns: Product_Name (truncated to 50 characters if needed), Category, Review_Count, and Avg_Rating (rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort by Avg_Rating descending, then Review_Count descending.

Create a Notion database called "Product Review Insights" with properties for Category (title), Product_Count (number), Review_Count (number), Avg_Rating (number), and Five_Star_Rate (number). Populate it with one entry per category from the Category Analysis sheet.

Email the analysis to product_team@store.com with subject "Product Review Analysis Report" and include a summary of which categories have the highest and lowest ratings in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two genuine dependency waves with exactly three sub-agents total. The first agent computes the complete store join once; the two artifact writers then run in parallel from one canonical category table.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Explore sub-agent:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Use one Explore sub-agent to retrieve the complete product and review endpoints read-only using `perPage=100` and increasing pages until each has a short or empty terminal page. Omit the optional review `status` argument, preserve every observed status, and filter only as the original task requires. Join strictly by Product_ID; a product contributes to each observed category exactly according to its source categories. Compute the compact per-category Product_Count, Review_Count, rating sum/average, Five_Star_Count/Rate, and the eligible products with at least three reviews. Rank Top Products by average rating descending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID. Return the full compact category and top-ten tables directly, plus endpoint page/row/status controls, join/category coverage, and duplicate/tie checks. Do not modify the store or create deliverables.

After Wave 1, the main agent independently checks the counts, rates, rankings, and tie order, then freezes one immutable category/top-product handoff for both writers.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 Coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole writer of `Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx`. Create the exact two sheets once from the frozen tables, with exact headers, truncation, sorting, row limits, rounding, and literal values. Read both sheets back and return the path plus complete row/value controls.

   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole owner of the exact-title `Product Review Insights` database. Search exact title once first and reuse an exact match, otherwise create the database once with the exact property types; then create exactly one page per frozen category, sending each page in a SINGLE create call that carries all its properties together — never update properties one at a time, never re-read pages between inserts, and do not verify row-by-row. When all rows are inserted, issue ONE final database query to confirm the row count, and return the database ID, property names and final row count. Do not write the workbook.

   3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole owner of the summary email to product_team@store.com with the exact task subject: body built ONLY from the frozen tables — the total product/review counts, the highest-rated and lowest-rated categories with their average ratings and five-star rates, and the complete per-category breakdown. Paginate Sent search and match the exact recipient/subject before an at-most-once send, then read the retained message back and return its ID. Do not write the workbook or database.

After all three writers return, reconcile every category across source, workbook, database and the sent message against the same frozen tables. Read back all three outputs. Repairs belong only to the original writer, and there is no separate validation wave.

After the final wave completes, do not invoke the agent-dispatch tool again — not even an empty or exploratory dispatch attempt (a dispatch that returns zero agents is wasted work). Any remaining checks, emails or small writes are main-agent direct work completed in one pass.

nodes.text:
You are working on a WooCommerce product-review analysis task. Your job: fetch all needed data, compute two summary tables, and produce an Excel file. Do NOT create any Notion database and do NOT send any email — the main agent will do those steps afterwards using your saved summary.

WORKSPACE: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-excel-notion/workspace
(You may read/write files only inside this directory. All relative paths below are relative to it.)

STEP 1 — Fetch all products from WooCommerce:
- Use mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=100 and paginate with page=1,2,3,... until an empty array [] is returned.
- IMPORTANT: A 100-product response is very large and may be truncated/oversized. If a response is truncated (you don't get complete JSON for every product, or you see a note about output exceeding size), instead re-fetch with smaller perPage values (e.g., 25 or 30) so each response is complete. Verify you have every product id exactly once.
- For each product record, extract: id, name, categories (array of {id, name}).
- Save all products as a JSON file "products.json" in the workspace.

STEP 2 — Fetch all product reviews:
- Use mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_reviews_list with perPage=100, paginating page=1,2,3,... until fewer than 100 results come back (i.e., the last page). The endpoint returns reviews ordered by id descending; review ids start at 396 and go down to 1 (396 reviews total, all status "approved").
- For each review extract: id, product_id, rating, status.
- Save all reviews as "reviews.json" in the workspace.
- Note: reviews may belong to product ids that appear in products.json; every review product_id should exist in products.json.

STEP 3 — Compute "Category Analysis":
- Categories (from mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_categories_list) are: Audio (id 1), Cameras (id 2), Electronics (id 3), Headphones (id 4), Home Appliances (id 5), Speakers (id 6), TV & Home Theater (id 7), Watches (id 8).
- A product may belong to MULTIPLE categories. For each category, a product counts toward Product_Count if the product's categories include that category id. A product's reviews count toward EVERY category the product belongs to.
- For each category compute:
  - Product_Count = number of distinct products in that category (all products, including ones with zero reviews).
  - Review_Count = total number of reviews across all products in that category.
  - Avg_Rating = mean of the review ratings in that category, rounded to 2 decimal places.
  - Five_Star_Count = number of reviews with rating == 5 in that category.
  - Five_Star_Rate = (Five_Star_Count / Review_Count) * 100, rounded to 1 decimal place. If Review_Count is 0, set to 0.
- Sort rows by Category name alphabetically (A-Z).

STEP 4 — Compute "Top Products":
- Only products with at least 3 reviews are eligible (use actual review counts from reviews.json, not the product's rating_count field).
- For each eligible product compute Review_Count and Avg_Rating (mean of its review ratings, rounded to 2 decimal places).
- Sort by Avg_Rating descending, then Review_Count descending; take the top 10.
- Product_Name = product name truncated to 50 characters if longer (truncate to exactly the first 50 characters). Category = the category name of the product (if the product has multiple categories, use the first category name listed in its categories array).
- Columns: Product_Name, Category, Review_Count, Avg_Rating.

STEP 5 — Create the Excel file:
- File: Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace.
- Sheet 1 named "Category Analysis" with header row: Category, Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating, Five_Star_Count, Five_Star_Rate. Include all 8 categories, sorted alphabetically. Write Avg_Rating values rounded to 2 decimals (e.g., 4.67) and Five_Star_Rate values rounded to 1 decimal (e.g., 62.5).
- Sheet 2 named "Top Products" with header row: Product_Name, Category, Review_Count, Avg_Rating. Include the top 10 rows.
- You may use mcp__excel__create_workbook / create_worksheet / write_data_to_excel, or build it with Python (openpyxl) via mcp__local__python_execute writing to the workspace path. Either way the final file must be at Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace. Delete the default "Sheet"/"Sheet1" if present so only the two required sheets remain.

STEP 6 — Save "summary.json" in the workspace containing:
{
  "category_analysis": [ {"Category": "...", "Product_Count": N, "Review_Count": N, "Avg_Rating": X.XX, "Five_Star_Count": N, "Five_Star_Rate": X.X}, ... sorted alphabetically ],
  "top_products": [ {"Product_Name": "...", "Category": "...", "Review_Count": N, "Avg_Rating": X.XX}, ... ],
  "stats": {"product_count": N, "review_count": N, "category_count": N}
}

VERIFICATION before you finish:
- Re-read your products.json and reviews.json and confirm: total distinct products, total reviews, and that the computed counts in summary.json are internally consistent (e.g., sum of per-category Review_Count equals total reviews if no product spans categories — if products span categories, that sum can exceed total reviews, which is expected).
- Confirm Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx exists with exactly two sheets named "Category Analysis" and "Top Products", and read it back to verify contents (use mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata and mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel).

REPORT BACK (concise but complete):
- The full category_analysis table (all 8 rows).
- The full top_products table (10 rows).
- Total products and total reviews found.
- The absolute path of Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx and summary.json.
- Any anomalies (products with no categories, reviews for unknown product ids, etc.).
Fetch WC data, build Excel
